children: CEO Brian Niccol said in a Bloomberg Television interview on Friday that the coffee chain could eventually expand beyond its core brand into a multi-brand business.
Asked about the possibility, Niccol called it “one of those possibilities,” adding that Starbucks’ scale provided an opportunity to go beyond being a one-brand company.
He said Starbucks’ immediate priority remained its internal growth strategy, which focused on upgrading stores, improving menus, and enhancing customer service.
However, he did not rule out a broader portfolio in the future, saying that adding other businesses that could leverage Starbucks’ strengths “could be an interesting proposition, down the road.”
He also said the company could meet its growth targets without acquisitions.
A multi-brand approach would resemble Yum! Brands
, which owns Taco Bell and KFC. His comments followed Starbucks’ October 12 denial that it was pursuing an acquisition of Chipotle Mexican Grill
, where Niccol previously served as CEO.

The comments came a day after the company reported fiscal fourth-quarter 2026 results. Global comparable sales rose 7.2%, while U.S. comparable sales increased 7.7%. Consolidated operating margin expanded 450 basis points YoY to 14%, while EPS grew approximately 54% to $0.80.
, Niccol said the results put Starbucks ahead of schedule on its fiscal 2028 framework.
On the market side, shares fell 1.18% to $104.26 on Friday.

title: Starbucks CEO: "I would never say never to a multi-brand future"
